prompt: explain how rising interest rates relate to prices

keyLinks.cause: The central bank raises its policy rate
keyLinks.effect: Interest rates on loans (and savings) across the economy rise
keyLinks.mechanism: The policy rate steers the short-term rates banks lend and borrow at, which feed into loan and deposit rates

keyLinks.cause: Borrowing costs more and saving pays more
keyLinks.effect: Households and businesses borrow and spend or invest less
keyLinks.mechanism: Loan-financed purchases get more expensive and holding money becomes more attractive

keyLinks.effect: Demand for goods and services falls
keyLinks.mechanism: Total spending in the economy is demand

keyLinks.effect: Businesses raise prices less (and wage growth slows)
keyLinks.mechanism: With fewer buyers, firms can't push prices up as easily without losing sales

keyLinks.cause: Price increases slow down across many businesses
keyLinks.effect: Inflation cools: prices keep rising but more slowly, usually after a lag of months to years
keyLinks.mechanism: Inflation is the rate at which the overall price level rises

keyLinks.cause: People expect the central bank to keep inflation down
keyLinks.effect: Smaller price and wage increases are set in advance
keyLinks.mechanism: Expectations feed into pricing and wage decisions

keyLinks.effect: The central bank stops raising or starts lowering rates (balancing loop)
keyLinks.mechanism: The central bank adjusts rates to steer inflation toward its target

knownErrors.claim: The normal outcome is that prices fall / the price level goes down
knownErrors.why: The usual effect is slower price growth (lower inflation), not falling prices

knownErrors.claim: Banks get (all) their money from the central bank at the policy rate, and that is the main reason loan rates rise
knownErrors.why: Misleading: the policy rate steers market interest rates; most bank funding is deposits and market borrowing

knownErrors.claim: The effect on prices is immediate
knownErrors.why: Monetary policy works with long and variable lags

knownErrors.claim: Higher rates mainly push prices up because businesses pass on higher loan costs
knownErrors.why: A cost channel exists but the main effect of higher rates is to cool demand and inflation

acceptableSimplifications: Talking about "the bank" or "loans" generically instead of market rates
Omitting exchange rates, asset prices and the expectations channel
Describing the outcome as "prices stop climbing so fast"
